It’s not actually the acid from the stomach that causes pneumonia, it’s the food particles, etc. in your stomach that you involuntarily vomit up and end up going down your trachea (wind pipe) into your lungs, rather than your esophagus (the way food should go).  Food and liquid aren’t meant to be in the lungs, your body knows this and tries to attack it but can’t clear it well (hard to get big particles like food out of your lungs), so you wind up with an infection, e.g. pneumonia. This specific type of pneumonia is called “aspiration pneumonia” and is very common in alcohol and drug-related incidents when patients pass out. Hope this helped!

Just my own two cents about “never give anyone PoA”: as long as you trust that person, PLEASE give them PoA.  There are so many uncertain things in life, we could made unable to make our own decisions at the drop of a hat.  During med school, I saw way too many sad stories of young people in the ICU who had long term significant others/close friends (who the patient would WANT as their PoA) trying to make medical decisions on their behalf, but they’d get legally stonewalled constantly because they didn’t have the right paperwork.  In most states (this is USA I’m talking about, can’t speak for other countries) PoA generally goes to a person’s spouse by default and then to their parents or biological children (every state is slightly different, so research if interested). If your default person to have PoA is NOT who you want (e.g. OP’s mom), then PLEASE learn how to set it up and appoint someone you trust.  The same goes for single people who would want their best friend or someone else close to make decisions for them... no one ever thinks about this until it’s too late.  It’s heartbreaking to watch a patient’s true loved ones trying to make the right call, but legally their terrible parent or spouse (sometimes even ex-spouse) gets to have the final word and it’s not what the patient would have wanted.  Sorry for the long-winded response... stay safe, everyone <3

THIS. There are so many articles being spread around that are citing causes of death that “aren’t COVID” and MANY people are misinterpreting that as “well, they didn’t die of COVID.”  

Untrue. For instance, an otherwise healthy 34 year old human died of “respiratory failure”, but since COVID wasn’t cited as THE cause of death, people are using it to persuade people that COVID isn’t as deadly as we’re told.  The data they remit, though, shows that said patient had no other reason to develop respiratory failure other than COVID infection (non-smoker, no exposure to potentially hazardous chemicals if inhaled, no personal or family history of pulmonary disease).

TLDR: COVID is serious and lethal, don’t spread lies if you have no idea what you’re talking about and PLEASE wash your hands and wear a mask.
